newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Saudi financier to operate Ethiopian gold mine.
newsitem.headline: Saudi financier to operate Ethiopian gold mine.

text.p: Ethiopian authorities said on Friday that an Ethiopian company owned by a Saudi Arabian financier had paid $175 million to take over operations of the country's only functioning gold-mine for some 20 years.

National Mining Corporation owned by Saudi Arabian Sheikh Mohamed Hussein Al Amoudi won the bid from among 13 international and local companies which tendered bids for Lege Dembi in the south of the Horn of African country, the Ethiopia News Agency (ENA) reported on Friday.

The company will have the right to produce and sell gold from deposits within an area of 85 sq km (52.7 sq miles) of the plant and was expected to increase output five times to 15 tonnes from the current three in a year, ENA reported.
No other details on the deal were immediately available.
Lege Dembi is situated in Ethiopia's Adola gold-belt some 300 kms (186 miles) south of the capital Addis Ababa.
Ethiopia, which says it has proven gold deposits of 500 tonnes, liberalised its mineral sector, opening up prospecting to private investement in 1993.
Eleven foreign firms have signed exploration agreements to seek gold and base metals in different regions since 1994.
